caption_hook: 🐯 Wild tigers are up 70% since 2010, 3 million mangroves are back in Nigeria, and 6 more wins from this week 👇
question: Which win made your week? Reply with its number, 1 to 8 👇
share_line: Save this for a day you need hope
first_comment: This week's picks span India, Hawaii, Brazil, Nigeria, Türkiye, deep space, France and Australia. Which country should we feature more? 🌍

stories.stat_label: wild tigers, up from about 3,200 in 2010
stories.headline: Wild tigers have bounced back by 70% since 2010
stories.summary: In 2010 only around 3,200 wild tigers were left. WWF's 2026 Living Planet Report says there are now roughly 5,700, after years of sustained conservation work.
stories.why: It shows protection works, even for a species that looked doomed.

stories.headline: Kilauea has shot 54 lava fountains, and now we know why
stories.summary: Since December 2024, Hawaii's Kilauea has fired 54 separate lava fountains, more often than ever recorded. USGS scientists found trapped gas pushes the magma up and down like a piston.
stories.why: Knowing what drives the fountains helps experts read the volcano's next move.

stories.headline: Rope bridges gave Amazon animals 15,000 safe road crossings
stories.summary: Eight canopy bridges strung over a road near Alta Floresta let spider monkeys, marmosets and capuchins cross 15,000 times in 15 months, with not a single roadkill recorded.
stories.why: A simple rope bridge keeps rare primates alive and their forest connected.

stories.headline: Women replant 3 million mangroves on oil-hit Niger Delta land
stories.summary: Since 2018, teams led by Martha Agbani have replanted 3 million mangroves and restored 190 hectares of swamp in oil-scarred Ogoniland. Fish and crabs are returning.
stories.why: Local women are healing their own land and getting their food and income back.

stories.headline: A lost Hittite royal archive is giving up its secrets
stories.summary: Archaeologists recovered 131 clay tablets and fragments this season at Kayalıpınar, ancient Šamuḫa. They tell of an epidemic, a princess's funeral and generals begging the king for help.
stories.why: We can now hear people from 3,400 years ago in their own words.

stories.stat_label: changing water clouds seen beyond us
stories.headline: Webb watched water clouds change on a world 7.5 light-years away
stories.summary: Webb tracked WISE 0855, the coldest known brown dwarf, for 11 hours. Its water clouds grew thicker and thinner: the first such weather confirmed beyond our solar system.
stories.why: It's like reading the weather report of another world.

stories.headline: Solar canopies boosted corn yields by almost 20% in a heatwave
stories.summary: In eastern France, where it topped 35°C for weeks, 5,500 solar panels raised 5 m over a maize field shaded the crop. Yields rose almost 20% versus open ground, while the panels made clean power.
stories.why: One field can now feed people and power homes, even as summers get hotter.

stories.headline: A family turned a mined-out reef island back into a bird haven
stories.summary: Guano mining in the 1860s left Lady Elliot Island bare for a century. From the 1960s the Adams family began replanting; now over 20,000 plants cover about 70% of it and seabirds nest again.
stories.why: Patient, hands-on work brought a whole ecosystem back to life.

fun_fact: Kilauea has been erupting almost continuously for nearly 200 years.
